Use computational Riemann-Roch theorem to convert this into Weierstrass curve.</span></p><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>## Main window</span></p><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>Two tinted surfaces with a slightly transparent shading, high quality rendering intersect along a red colored algebraic curve</span></p><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>Rotation with mouses in both directions, full pinch mechanism for zoom, haptic press to show the little menu with sliders for changing the coefficients of each surface; detection via Z-buffor level</span></p><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>## Side right window</span></p><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>Short Weierstrass equation (over Q or quadratic field extension) computed on the go via effective Riemann-Roch theorem formulas</span></p><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>## Ambient mode where all the controls are hidden and the user can admire the beauty of the shapes</span></p><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>## Specs</span></p><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>App is running in the browser, light-weight implementation with full stack newest libraries, portable, deployable</span></p><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>## Docs</span></p><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>Git repo, journal, plan (Markdown files)</span></p></div></div><button type="button" class="text-caption text-primary-60">Show more</button></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="col-span-12 group [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-xl [&:not(:last-child)]:mb-xl"><div class="max-w-container multi-columns:px-0 @container w-full"><div class="px-sm grid grid-cols-12 gap-y-8"><blockquote class="text-h3 text-primary-100 col-span-12 col-start-1 text-center font-medium tracking-tight @md:col-span-8 @md:col-start-3">“It’s incredibly energizing to use OpenAI’s new GPT-5.5 model in our harness, have it reason over massive biochemical datasets to predict human drug outcomes, and then see it deliver significant accuracy gains on our hardest drug discovery evals. If OpenAI keeps cooking like this, the foundations of drug discovery will change by the end of the year.”</blockquote><div class="text-primary-100 text-meta col-span-12 col-start-1 text-center text-pretty @md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4">— Brandon White, Co-Founder & CEO at Axiom Bio</div></div></div></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-xl"><div class="max-w-container @container grid w-full grid-cols-12 toc-content-heading scroll-mt-[calc(var(--header-h)+var(--toc-button-h))]" id="next-generation-inference-efficiency"><div class="full-grid-content:@md:col-span-12 full-grid-content:@md:col-start-1 col-span-12 max-w-none @md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4"><h2 class="text-h3 scroll-mt-[calc(var(--header-h)+var(--toc-button-h))]"><span>Next-generation inference efficiency</span></h2></div></div></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-sm"><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>Serving GPT‑5.5 at GPT‑5.4 latency required rethinking inference as an integrated system, not a set of isolated optimizations. GPT‑5.5 was co-designed for, trained with, and served on NVIDIA GB200 and GB300 NVL72 systems. Codex and GPT‑5.5 were instrumental in how we achieved our performance targets. Codex helped the team move faster from idea to benchmarkable implementation, sketching approaches, wiring experiments, and helping identify which optimizations were worth deeper investment. GPT‑5.5 helped find and implement key improvements in the stack itself. Put simply, the model helped improve the infrastructure that serves it.</span></p></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-sm"><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>One such improvement was load balancing and partitioning heuristics. Before GPT‑5.5, we split requests on an accelerator into a fixed number of chunks to balance work across computing cores, ensuring big and small requests could run on the same GPU. However, a pre-determined number of static chunks is not optimal for all traffic shapes. To better utilize GPUs, Codex analyzed weeks’ worth of production traffic patterns and wrote custom heuristic algorithms to optimally partition and balance work. The effort had an outsized impact, increasing token generation speeds by over 20%.</span></p></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-xl"><div class="max-w-container @container grid w-full grid-cols-12 toc-content-heading scroll-mt-[calc(var(--header-h)+var(--toc-button-h))]" id="advancing-cybersecurity-for-everyones-safety"><div class="full-grid-content:@md:col-span-12 full-grid-content:@md:col-start-1 col-span-12 max-w-none @md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4"><h2 class="text-h3 scroll-mt-[calc(var(--header-h)+var(--toc-button-h))]"><span>Advancing cybersecurity for everyone’s safety</span></h2></div></div></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-sm"><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>Preparing the world for models that are very good at finding and patching security vulnerabilities is a team sport and will require the entire ecosystem to work hard to build resilience, with democratized model access and iterative deployment for the </span><a class="transition ease-curve-a duration-250 text-primary-100 hover:text-primary-60 relative underline-offset-[0.25rem] decoration-1 underline" href="/index/scaling-trusted-access-for-cyber-defense/"><span>next era of cyber defense</span>⁠</a><span>.</span></p></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-sm"><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>Frontier models are becoming increasingly more capable in cybersecurity. Those capabilities will become broadly distributed and we believe the best path forward is to make sure they can be put to use for accelerating cyber defense and strengthening the ecosystem.</span></p></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-sm"><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>GPT‑5.5 is an incremental but important step towards AI that can solve some of the world’s toughest challenges like cybersecurity. With GPT‑5.2 in December, we proactively deployed the necessary </span><a class="transition ease-curve-a duration-250 text-primary-100 hover:text-primary-60 relative underline-offset-[0.25rem] decoration-1 underline" href="/index/strengthening-cyber-resilience/"><span>cyber safeguards</span>⁠</a><span> to limit potential cyber abuse with our models; now with GPT‑5.5, we’re deploying stricter classifiers for potential cyber risk which some users may find annoying initially, as we tune them over time. </span></p></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-sm"><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>We’ve identified cybersecurity as a category in our </span><a href="https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf" class="transition ease-curve-a duration-250 text-primary-100 hover:text-primary-60 relative underline-offset-[0.25rem] decoration-1 underline" target="_blank" referrerpolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"><span>Preparedness Framework</span>⁠<span class="sr-only">(opens in a new window)</span></a><span> for years as our models have incrementally improved, while we develop and calibrate mitigations iteratively, to be able to responsibly release models with meaningful cybersecurity capabilities.</span></p></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-sm"><ul class="mb-md marker:text-inherit last:mb-0 in-[:where(ul,ol)]:mt-2 list-disc in-[:where(ul,ol)]:list-[circle] ps-2xs mx-3xs"><li class="mb-4xs"><b><span>We are deploying industry-leading safeguards for this level of cyber capability. </span></b><span>We first introduced cyber-specific safeguards with </span><a href="https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-5-2/deception" class="transition ease-curve-a duration-250 text-primary-100 hover:text-primary-60 relative underline-offset-[0.25rem] decoration-1 underline" target="_blank" referrerpolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"><span>GPT‑5.2</span>⁠<span class="sr-only">(opens in a new window)</span></a><span> last year, which we have continued to test, refine, and build on in subsequent deployments. For GPT‑5.5, we designed tighter controls around higher-risk activity, sensitive cyber requests, and added protections for repeated misuse. Broad access is made possible through our investments in model safety, authenticated usage, and monitoring for impermissible use. We have been working with external experts for months to develop, test and iterate on the robustness of these safeguards. With GPT‑5.5, we are ensuring developers can secure their code with ease, while putting stronger controls around the cyber workflows most likely to cause harm by malicious actors.</span></li><li class="mb-4xs"><b><span>We are expanding access to accelerate cyber defense at every level. </span></b><span>We are making our cyber-permissive models available through </span><a class="transition ease-curve-a duration-250 text-primary-100 hover:text-primary-60 relative underline-offset-[0.25rem] decoration-1 underline" href="/index/scaling-trusted-access-for-cyber-defense/"><span>Trusted Access for Cyber</span>⁠</a><span>, starting with Codex, which includes expanded access to the advanced cybersecurity capabilities of GPT‑5.5 with fewer restrictions for verified users meeting certain </span><a href="https://developers.openai.com/codex/concepts/cyber-safety" class="transition ease-curve-a duration-250 text-primary-100 hover:text-primary-60 relative underline-offset-[0.25rem] decoration-1 underline" target="_blank" referrerpolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"><span>trust signals</span>⁠<span class="sr-only">(opens in a new window)</span></a><span> at launch. Organizations who are responsible for </span><a class="transition ease-curve-a duration-250 text-primary-100 hover:text-primary-60 relative underline-offset-[0.25rem] decoration-1 underline" href="/index/accelerating-cyber-defense-ecosystem/"><span>defending critical infrastructure</span>⁠</a><span> can apply to access cyber-permissive models like GPT‑5.4‑Cyber, while meeting strict security requirements to use these models for securing their internal systems. This gives a wide range of verified defenders more capable tools for legitimate security work with less unnecessary friction to ensure we democratize access to important defensive capabilities. Users can apply for trusted access at </span><a href="http://chatgpt.com/cyber?openaicom-did=4da423c6-8c57-4bfd-a96f-67ed5db74ee8&openaicom_referred=true" class="transition ease-curve-a duration-250 text-primary-100 hover:text-primary-60 relative underline-offset-[0.25rem] decoration-1 underline" target="_blank" referrerpolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"><span>chatgpt.com/cyber</span>⁠<span class="sr-only">(opens in a new window)</span></a><span> to reduce unnecessary refusals while using GPT‑5.5 for verified defensive work.</span></li><li class="mb-4xs"><b><span>We are working with government partners to help protect critical infrastructure for the public. </span></b><span>Together, we are exploring how advanced AI can support the defensive work of trusted officials responsible for systems people rely on, from the digital systems that secure important taxpayer data to the power grid and water supplies in local communities.</span></li></ul></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-sm"><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>We are treating the biological/chemical and cybersecurity capabilities of GPT‑5.5 as High under our </span><a href="https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf" class="transition ease-curve-a duration-250 text-primary-100 hover:text-primary-60 relative underline-offset-[0.25rem] decoration-1 underline" target="_blank" referrerpolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"><span>Preparedness Framework</span>⁠<span class="sr-only">(opens in a new window)</span></a><span>. While GPT‑5.5 didn’t reach Critical cybersecurity capability level, our evaluations and testing showed that its cybersecurity capabilities are a step up compared to GPT‑5.4.</span></p></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-sm"><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>In addition, GPT‑5.5 went through our full safety and governance process prior to release, including preparedness evaluations, domain-specific testing, new targeted evaluations for advanced biology and cybersecurity capabilities, and robust testing with external experts. We share more details in the GPT‑5.5 </span><a href="https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/gpt-5-5" class="transition ease-curve-a duration-250 text-primary-100 hover:text-primary-60 relative underline-offset-[0.25rem] decoration-1 underline" target="_blank" referrerpolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"><span>system card</span>⁠<span class="sr-only">(opens in a new window)</span></a><span>.</span></p></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-sm"><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>This work reflects our broader AI resilience approach, which we believe is needed as model capabilities advance. We want powerful AI to be available to the people using it to defend systems, institutions, and the public. The viable path is trusted access, robust safeguards that scale with capability, and the operational capacity to detect and respond to serious misuse.</span></p></div><div class="col-span-12 group [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-xl [&:not(:last-child)]:mb-xl"><figure class="max-w-container @container grid w-full grid-cols-12"><div class="gap-sm col-span-12 flex min-h-0 flex-col @md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4"><div class="gap-sm flex min-h-0 w-full min-w-0 flex-col @sm:flex-row items-start"><div class="h-[400px]"></div></div></div></figure></div><div class="col-span-12 group [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-xl [&:not(:last-child)]:mb-xl"><figure class="max-w-container @container grid w-full grid-cols-12"><div class="gap-sm col-span-12 flex min-h-0 flex-col @md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4"><div class="gap-sm flex min-h-0 w-full min-w-0 flex-col @sm:flex-row items-start"><div class="h-[400px]"></div></div></div></figure></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-xl"><div class="max-w-container @container grid w-full grid-cols-12 toc-content-heading scroll-mt-[calc(var(--header-h)+var(--toc-button-h))]" id="availability-and-pricing"><div class="full-grid-content:@md:col-span-12 full-grid-content:@md:col-start-1 col-span-12 max-w-none @md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4"><h2 class="text-h3 scroll-mt-[calc(var(--header-h)+var(--toc-button-h))]"><span>Availability and pricing</span></h2></div></div></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-sm"><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>Today, GPT‑5.5 is rolling out to Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in ChatGPT and Codex, and GPT‑5.5 Pro is rolling out to Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in ChatGPT. We'll bring GPT‑5.5 and GPT‑5.5 Pro to the API very soon.</span></p></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-sm"><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>In ChatGPT, GPT‑5.5 Thinking is available to Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users. GPT‑5.5 Pro, designed for even harder questions and higher-accuracy work, is available to Pro, Business, and Enterprise users.</span></p></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-sm"><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>In Codex, GPT‑5.5 is available for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, Edu, and Go plans with a 400K context window. GPT‑5.5 is also available in Fast mode, generating tokens 1.5x faster for 2.5x the cost. </span></p></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-sm"><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>For API developers, gpt-5.5 will soon be available in the Responses and Chat Completions APIs at $5 per 1M input tokens and $30 per 1M output tokens, with a 1M context window. Batch and Flex pricing are available at half the standard API rate, while Priority processing is available at 2.5x the standard rate. We will also release gpt-5.5-pro in the API for even higher accuracy, priced at $30 per 1M input tokens and $180 per 1M output tokens. See the </span><a class="transition ease-curve-a duration-250 text-primary-100 hover:text-primary-60 relative underline-offset-[0.25rem] decoration-1 underline" href="/api/pricing/"><span>pricing page</span>⁠</a><span> for full details.</span></p></div><div class="@md:col-span-6 @md:col-start-4 col-span-12 max-w-none [&:not(:first-child)]:mt-sm"><p class="mb-sm last:mb-0"><span>While GPT‑5.5 is priced higher than GPT‑5.4, it is both more intelligent and much more token efficient.
